package_info.package_name: Mercedes Me Connect / SiriusXM Connected Vehicle Services (infrastructure and apps)
package_info.package_versions: Not specified; all versions using the vulnerable SSO and cloud infrastructure
package_info.why_malicious: The infrastructure and applications expose sensitive internal development environments, source code, and cloud resources due to authentication and access control flaws. This allows unauthorized users to register accounts with broad internal access, leading to potential supply chain compromise, remote code execution, privilege escalation, and exfiltration of sensitive data.

execution_context.trigger: user registration via public repair shop portal

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Public registration page for repair shops writes to the same database as the core employee LDAP system, allowing non-employees to create accounts with broad internal access.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During user registration via the public portal, the application writes new user data to the central LDAP directory, granting SSO credentials that provide access to internal SSO-protected resources, including source code repositories and internal tools.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The registration process allows external users to create accounts in the same LDAP directory as employees, bypassing expected internal vetting and enabling unauthorized access.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal behavior would restrict internal access to verified employees only, with external users isolated from sensitive systems. Here, external users can escalate privileges and access internal resources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate repair shops may require limited access to certain external-facing systems, but should never be able to register for broad internal access or source code repositories.
key_indicators: Public registration writes directly to employee LDAP directory
No separation between external and internal user privileges in LDAP
SSO tokens issued to unvetted external users

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Newly created user credentials from the public registration portal allow login to internal GitHub repositories containing sensitive source code and documentation.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After SSO login with credentials obtained via public registration, the user accesses internal GitHub repositories, enabling download and viewing of sensitive source code and internal documentation.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: External users, who should not have access, can authenticate and access internal source code repositories, exposing proprietary code and documentation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Source code repositories are expected to be restricted to vetted developers and internal staff; here, any registered user can access them without additional verification.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; only internal developers and authorized personnel should have access to these repositories.
key_indicators: SSO credentials from public registration grant access to internal code repositories
No access control separation between internal and external users in repository permissions
Repository access logs show new, unrecognized users

execution_context.file_location: Internal cloud deployment services, Jenkins, AWS control panels

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: SSO credentials allow access to cloud deployment panels, Jenkins, AWS, and internal APIs, enabling remote code execution and management of internal systems.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: After SSO login, the user can access cloud management interfaces (Jenkins, AWS control panels), request and manage internal systems, and execute code or administrative actions on internal infrastructure.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: External users can perform administrative actions on critical infrastructure, including code execution and system management, which should be restricted to trusted employees.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Only trusted, authenticated employees should have access to cloud and CI/CD management panels; external users should be blocked or require additional verification.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; this level of access is reserved for internal cloud administrators and DevOps personnel.
key_indicators: SSO tokens from public registration grant cloud admin access
No privilege separation or additional verification for sensitive cloud resources
Access logs show new users performing administrative actions

execution_context.trigger: source code analysis or reverse engineering of client apps

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: JavaScript bundles contain hardcoded API endpoints and sensitive credentials/constants, exposing backend API routes and sometimes credentials.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During reverse engineering or runtime analysis, the JavaScript code reveals hardcoded backend API endpoints and sensitive constants, allowing attackers to identify and target backend systems directly, and potentially use exposed credentials for unauthorized access.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Sensitive credentials and internal API routes are exposed in client-side code, making it trivial for attackers to discover and exploit backend services.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Production client code should never contain secrets or internal endpoints; such information should be securely stored and never exposed to end users.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: API endpoints may be exposed for legitimate client-server communication, but credentials and sensitive constants should never be present in client-side code.
key_indicators: Hardcoded credentials or tokens in JavaScript bundles
Internal API routes and endpoints visible in client code
Sensitive constants (e.g., API keys, secrets) present in distributed app code

execution_context.trigger: cloud storage access using compromised credentials

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Leaked AWS keys provide full organizational read/write access to S3 buckets, exposing user databases, source code, and config files.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: With compromised AWS keys, an attacker can authenticate to AWS S3, list, read, and modify all files in S3 buckets, enabling exfiltration of sensitive data and potential tampering with production assets.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Full S3 access via leaked AWS keys allows attackers to exfiltrate and tamper with critical organizational data, including user databases and source code.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: AWS keys should be tightly controlled, rotated, and never exposed in code or client applications; only trusted cloud admins should have this level of access.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Only trusted cloud administrators should have full S3 access; application-level access should be limited and scoped.
key_indicators: Leaked AWS keys found in code or configuration files
Full S3 bucket access permissions granted to non-admin users
Unusual S3 access patterns from new or external accounts

attack_chain.action: Register a new user via the public Mercedes repair shop portal, which writes user data to the central LDAP directory and issues SSO credentials.
attack_chain.leads_to: Obtain SSO credentials with internal access

attack_chain.action: Use SSO credentials to access internal GitHub repositories and source code.
Leverage SSO credentials to access cloud deployment panels, Jenkins, AWS, and internal APIs.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution and infrastructure control

attack_chain.action: Extract sensitive API endpoints and credentials from JavaScript bundles in web/mobile apps.
attack_chain.leads_to: Direct backend API attacks and further data exfiltration

attack_chain.action: Use leaked AWS keys to access and exfiltrate all files from SiriusXM S3 buckets.
attack_chain.leads_to: Full compromise of user databases, source code, and configuration files

behavioral_signatures: External user registration resulting in issuance of internal SSO credentials
Access to internal GitHub or cloud management panels by accounts registered via public portals
Download or viewing of sensitive source code or documentation by newly created or unrecognized accounts
Extraction or presence of hardcoded credentials and internal API endpoints in client-side JavaScript bundles
Unusual or large-scale S3 bucket access, including mass downloads or modifications by accounts with recently issued AWS keys
file_indicators: Public registration portals (e.g., umas.mercedes-benz.com/orgprocess/#) writing to employee LDAP directories
JavaScript bundles in web/mobile apps containing hardcoded credentials or internal API endpoints
AWS keys or secrets present in source code repositories or configuration files
network_indicators: SSO login attempts from external or previously unseen IP addresses to internal resources
API calls to internal endpoints from accounts registered via public portals
Large data transfers or unusual access patterns from S3 buckets to unfamiliar destinations or IPs
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for new user registrations from public portals that result in SSO credentials with internal access. Alert on access to source code repositories, cloud management panels, or sensitive documentation by accounts not previously seen or registered externally. Scan client-side JavaScript bundles for hardcoded credentials or internal API endpoints. Audit AWS key usage for anomalous access patterns, especially mass downloads, access from new locations, or use of keys found in source code.
